text: Shared page chrome rules (owner asked for consistency across the app, STA-660): (1) every page title (h1.pt) sits inside the .pagehead wrapper, which alone sets the 10px gap below the title; do not add per-page margins to fix title spacing. The design files show a bare h1 on notifications, new thread and comment form; the app wraps them on purpose. (2) Form errors use one style, the bordered .err box; the plain red-text .error class was removed. Considered and left alone by owner choice: the three empty-state text styles (normal text for 'No threads/notifications/results', grey for 'No comments yet', small mono hint for 'no invite links').
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Public mode scope (agreed with the owner, STA-644): visitors get read-only access to the thread list, threads and search only. Deliberately NOT public: the invite tree (/tree, /invites) because it exposes who invited whom; live SSE updates for visitors (avoid long-lived anonymous connections); per-thread visibility (rejected: turning public on retroactively exposes all old threads, accepted with a warning on the settings page instead); user profile pages (not built, would be a separate ticket). Settings live in the DB and are edited by admins rather than flags, because the owner wanted changes without a restart.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: When @mention highlighting was added to the Markdown renderer (STA-640), stored body_html of old posts was NOT re-rendered, because the user confirmed no production server with real posts existed at the time. If highlights are missing on old posts in some database, that is why; a one-time re-render of threads.body_html and comments.body_html would fix it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The design in misc/design shows the footer as 'soliloquy v1.0 · AGPL-3.0 · source · invite tree'. The app deliberately shows only 'powered by soliloquy', linked to the GitHub repo (owner decision, STA-656). Reasons: the version was hardcoded and always wrong, the invite tree link duplicates the main nav, and the GitHub link already covers source and license. Rejected: a real build version via -ldflags or debug.ReadBuildInfo (build plumbing for little value). The footer still shows only to logged-in users. Do not restore the old items just because the design shows them.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The front page design (misc/design/00-front-page and the mobile screen) shows 'sorted by latest activity · page N' next to the ~/threads heading, and a mobile row 'latest activity / page N'. Both were deliberately removed (owner decision, STA-656): there is only one sort order, and the page number repeats the bottom bar. The bottom pagination bar ('page N of M · 30 per page' with newer/older buttons) is also hidden when there is no other page to go to, because it then has no buttons. Do not restore these labels just because the design shows them.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The design in misc/design shows a 'mark all as read' button on the notifications page. It was deliberately left out (user decision, STA-640): opening the page keeps marking everything read, and the 'unread' section shows what was unread before the visit. Rejected alternative: mark one item read only on click, plus the button; it needs a GET link that changes data and adds a step for users. Do not add the button just because the design shows it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The account (misc/design/07-account, 720px), notifications (03, 820px), search (04, 780px, centred) and comment form (820px) pages had narrower columns in the design. The app deliberately uses the normal 960px page column on all of them, so their boxes are as wide as the admin pages and header (owner decision, STA-660). The narrower caps were mostly left-aligned, which left empty space on the right and looked broken. Rejected: centring the narrow columns to match the design (the owner wanted full width). Not changed: the 72ch reading width of thread bodies and the 280px password inputs. Do not restore the narrow caps just because the design shows them.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Discord integration scope (agreed with the owner, STA-659): every new thread (not only link threads) posts one plain-text message to each admin-configured webhook URL; multiple webhooks were requested by the owner. Body is included but cut to 300 characters because the owner did not want Discord to be spammy. Plain text chosen over Discord embeds for simplicity. Deliberately NOT built: posting comments, edits or deletes; retries or a delivery queue (a lost message is acceptable); per-webhook options; Slack/generic webhooks; a host allowlist (only admins set URLs). Webhooks are configured in DB settings, not env vars, to match the no-restart rule in bedjup. The message does not include the external URL of link threads (STA-661): the owner wants Discord members to visit the forum to see the link and talk about it there.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Favicon and OG image (STA-647, user decision): one static text-free mark (amber chevron + cursor on #0f110e) for all forums. Rejected: baking 'soliloquy' into og.png (wrong after an admin renames the forum); rendering a per-forum OG image in Go (needs a TTF font, a font dependency and a handler, too much for a preview image); a favicon SVG that switches colours with the system theme (the ICO/PNG cannot switch, fixed dark tile reads fine on both). No og:description on purpose: the app has no description text and a fixed sentence would be wrong for most forums.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The desktop design (misc/design/05-invites-and-invite-tree.png) shows the 'invite someone' and 'your links' panels both below the invite tree. The app deliberately puts 'invite someone' above the tree and keeps 'your links' below it (owner decision, STA-649): the tree grows with each member and would push the main action of the page down. Rejected: a sidebar next to the tree (too cramped in the 960px page, even after widening it from 280px to 320px); both panels above the tree (the link history grows and would push the tree down). The same order is used on mobile. The mobile design (13) has no 'your links' list and a different invite box style; matching that was left out of scope.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Admins can edit any thread (title, URL, body) but NOT comments (owner decision, STA-654): the main need is fixing bad titles, and editing other people's comments has more room for abuse. Admin edits show only 'edited' with no editor name; an 'edited by admin' marker (needs a DB column) was deferred until it is a real problem. Thread edit/delete sit in the meta line ('2 comments · edited · edit · delete'); the design has no thread controls, and the owner finds 'edited' next to the controls a bit odd but accepted it for now.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
